title: Item-total correlations and alpha-if-item-removed diagnostics — alpha_diagnostics
text: Computes item-level reliability diagnostics unidimensional   scale. item function returns corrected uncorrected   item-total correlations Cronbach's alpha recalculated item   excluded. Use alongside raw_alpha identify items   reduce scale reliability.

title: Item-total correlations and alpha-if-item-removed diagnostics — alpha_diagnostics

text: df data frame whose columns items single scale. columns must numeric.

title: Item-total correlations and alpha-if-item-removed diagnostics — alpha_diagnostics
text: data frame one row per item following columns: item Item name. alpha..item.removed Cronbach's alpha computed remaining       items excluding item. item.total.correlation Pearson correlation item       sum items (uncorrected). item.total.correlation.r.drop Pearson correlation       item sum items (corrected item-total correlation,       also known r-drop). Values 0.30 typically indicate       problematic item.

Check dataframe — cdf
text: Produces column-level diagnostic summary dataframe, reporting missing values, data types, range statistics, optionally unique values factor levels. Returns named list per-column table whole-dataframe summary. Can optionally export results .xlsx file.

title: Check dataframe — cdf
code: cdf(   df,   name_length = (getOption("width")/3),   digits = 2,   nuniques = 0,   parralel = FALSE,   file = NULL )

title: Check dataframe — cdf
text: df data.frame inspect. Accepts column types: numeric, integer, character, factor, logical, Date, POSIXct. name_length Integer. Maximum number characters displayed column names MIN/MAX values printed output. Longer strings truncated. Defaults getOption("width") / 3. digits Integer. Number decimal places used rounding MEAN, MEDIAN, SD numeric columns. Defaults 2. nuniques Integer. > 0, appends UNIQUES LEVELS columns output. Columns distinct entries nuniques summarised "N Uniques" / "N Levels". Set 0 skip (faster). Defaults 0. parralel Logical. TRUE, uses future.apply multisession plan across available cores. Recommended wide dataframes (> 100 columns) large n. Defaults FALSE. file Character NULL. string provided, exports results <file>.xlsx two sheets: variables summary. existing file name overwritten. Defaults NULL.

title: Check dataframe — cdf
text: named list two elements: $summary single-row data.frame whole-dataframe     counts: COLLUMNS, ROWS, TOTAL, EMPTY, null, NAN, na, INF, FIN, FACTOR. $check per-column data.frame following     fields: NAMES Column name (truncated name_length). EMPTY Count "" empty strings. null Count NULL values (always 0 dataframe columns). na Count NA values. NOT_NA Count non-NA values. NAN Count NaN values. INF Count Inf -Inf values. FIN Count finite values. RANGE Number distinct values. MEAN Arithmetic mean, rounded digits. NA non-numeric columns. MEDIAN Median, rounded digits. NA non-numeric columns. SD Standard deviation, rounded digits. NA non-numeric columns. MIN Minimum value first label sorted order. MAX Maximum value last label sorted order. MODE Storage mode returned mode(). TYPE Type returned typeof(). CLASS Class returned class(). FACTOR Logical; TRUE column factor.

title: Check dataframe — cdf
text: MEAN, MEDIAN, SD NA non-numeric columns. MIN   MAX non-double columns derived sort() character   representations — natural sort ordering guaranteed mixed   alphanumeric strings.

title: Check dataframe (optimised) — cdff
text: faster equivalent cdf. Produces identical column-level diagnostic summary avoids repeated passes column, eliminates row--row rbind calls, removes gtools plyr dependencies. Recommended large dataframes (> 100k rows > 50 columns).

title: Check dataframe (optimised) — cdff
text: df data.frame inspect. Accepts column types: numeric, integer, character, factor, logical, Date, POSIXct. name_length Integer. Maximum number characters displayed column names MIN/MAX values printed output. Longer strings truncated. Defaults getOption("width") / 3. digits Integer. Number decimal places used rounding MEAN, MEDIAN, SD numeric columns. Defaults 2. nuniques Integer. > 0, appends UNIQUES LEVELS columns output. Columns distinct entries nuniques summarised "N Uniques" / "N Levels". Set 0 skip (faster). Defaults 0. parralel Logical. TRUE, uses future.apply multisession plan across available cores. Recommended wide dataframes (> 100 columns) large n. Defaults FALSE. file Character NULL. string provided, exports results <file>.xlsx two sheets: variables summary. existing file name overwritten. Defaults NULL.

title: Check for Heywood Cases and Related SEM Estimation Problems — check_heywood
text: Screens fitted lavaan model common warning signs   negative variances, impossible standardized values, unusually large   standard errors, convergence failure. simple terms:   quick model health check. tells whether solution   contains suspicious estimates often indicate misspecification,   weak identification, numerical instability.

title: Check for Heywood Cases and Related SEM Estimation Problems — check_heywood
Check for Heywood Cases and Related SEM Estimation Problems — check_heywood
text: fit_model fitted lavaan model object (example, lavaan::cfa(), lavaan::sem(), related wrappers). verbose Logical. TRUE (default), prints diagnostic sections summary console. FALSE, returns results.

title: Check for Heywood Cases and Related SEM Estimation Problems — check_heywood
text: invisible list : has_issues: Logical, TRUE issue detected. issues: Named list detected issue tables/messages. converged: Logical convergence flag     lavaan::lavInspect(fit_model, "converged").

title: Check for Heywood Cases and Related SEM Estimation Problems — check_heywood
text: function checks: Negative variances (~~ lhs == rhs estimate < 0). Negative residual variances Thurstonian style parameters     (~*~ estimate < 0). Standardized loadings outside [-1, 1]. Standardized correlations outside [-1, 1]. Extremely large standard errors (se > 10). Non-convergence. Heywood case usually refers impossible estimates like negative variances standardized loadings greater 1 absolute value.

title: Proportion overall accuracy of a confusion matrix — proportion_accurate
text: function evaluates performance confusion matrix calculating overall accuracy Cohen's kappa statistics. function performs following steps: 1. Computes confusion matrix observed predicted values. 2. Calculates diagonal proportion (overall accuracy) -diagonal proportion. 3. Computes Cohen's kappa statistics (unweighted,linear,squared weights). output data.frame containing following metrics: -`cm_diagonal`: Proportion correct classifications (diagonal elements). -`cm_off_diagonal`: Proportion misclassified observations (-diagonal elements). -`kappa_unweighted`: Cohen's kappa statistic weights. -`kappa_linear`: Cohen's kappa statistic linear weights. -`kappa_squared`: Cohen's kappa statistic squared weights.

text: Pillai-Bartlett trace (V): Represents sum proportion explained variance discriminant functions. ,similar ratio SS M /SS T,known R 2.  Hotelling-s T 2: Represents sum eigenvalues variate compares directly F-ratio ANOVA   Wilks-s lambda (L): Represents ratio error variance total variance (SS R /SS T ) variate.   Roy-s largest root: Represents proportion explained variance unexplained variance (SS M /SS R ) first discriminant function.   ASSUMPTIONS   Independence: Observations statistically independent.   Random sampling: Data randomly sampled population interest measured interval level.   Multivariate normality: ANOVA,assume dependent variable normally distributed within group. case MANOVA,assume dependent variables (collectively) multivariate normality within groups.   Homogeneity covariance matrices: ANOVA,assumed variances group roughly equal (homogeneity variance). MANOVA must assume true dependent variable,also correlation two dependent variables groups. assumption examined testing whether population variance-covariance matrices different groups analysis equal.

text: Plots time series overlays family smoothed curves   using chosen smoothing method. bandwidth-based methods   ("kernel", "lowess", "splines", "default"),   sequence bandwidth span values start stop   swept curve drawn different rainbow colour, making   easy visually select appropriate smoothing level.   "polynomial" "linear" ignore bandwidth sequence   fit regression-based trend lines instead. function uses base R   graphics produces plot side effect.

title: Time series smoothing with multiple bandwidth levels — ts_smoothing
text: df ts object containing time series smooth. start Numeric. Starting value bandwidth span sequence. Default 0.01. stop Numeric. Ending value bandwidth span sequence. Default 2. step Numeric. Increment bandwidth values. Smaller values produce curves. Default 0.001. title Character string appended plot title. Default "". type Character string specifying smoothing method. One : "kernel" Gaussian kernel smoother via ksmooth() — bandwidth controls smoothing window (default). "lowess" Locally weighted regression via lowess() — f controls span proportion. "friedman" Friedman's super-smoother via supsmu() — span must (0, 1). "splines" Smoothing splines via smooth.spline() — spar controls penalty. "default" Running mean filter via filter() — bandwidth rounded integer window width. "polynomial" Fits centred cubic polynomial trend without seasonal (cos/sin) terms via lm(). "linear" Fits simple linear trend via lm() draws regression line.

title: Time series smoothing with multiple bandwidth levels — ts_smoothing
